# Linear algebra

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## Array extensions where Element == [Double]

- `func solve(_ b: [Double]) -> [Double]?` — Solves the linear system `A · x = b` for the unknown vector `x`. Returns: The solution vector `x`, or `nil` if `self` is not square, has rows of inconsistent length, has a row count that disagrees with `b.count`, or is singular (no unique solution). *(since 1.1.0)*
- `func luDecomposed() throws -> LUDecomposition` — Factors a square matrix into `P · A = L · U` using partial pivoting. Returns: The `L`, `U`, and permutation factors of the matrix. Throws: `MatrixError.notSquare` if the matrix is not square or has rows of inconsistent length; `MatrixError.singular` if the matrix is singular. *(since 1.5.0)*
- `func eigenDecomposed() throws -> EigenDecomposition` — Computes the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix. Returns: The eigenvalues (descending) and matching eigenvectors. Throws: `MatrixError.notSquare` if the matrix is empty, non-square, or has rows of inconsistent length; `MatrixError.notSymmetric` if any off-diagonal pair differs beyond the relative tolerance. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `func covarianceMatrix(ddof: Int = 1) -> [[Double]]?` — Computes the covariance matrix of a design matrix whose rows are samples and columns are features. Returns: A p × p symmetric covariance matrix, or `nil` if the array is empty, the rows have inconsistent lengths, `ddof` is negative, or there are fewer than `ddof + 1` rows. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `func asExpression() -> String` — Returns the matrix as a string, with each cell formatted by `UnicodeMath.formatCell` and each column right-aligned to its widest entry. Returns: The matrix as a Unicode-formatted multi-line string. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func asFractions(maxDenominator: Int = 1000) -> [[Fraction]]` — Converts each element to its simplest fractional representation. Returns: A 2D array of `Fraction` values

## LUDecomposition

`struct LUDecomposition` — The result of an LU factorization with partial pivoting. *(since 1.5.0)*

- `let l: [[Double]]` — Unit lower triangular factor (1s on the diagonal, multipliers below). *(since 1.5.0)*
- `let u: [[Double]]` — Upper triangular factor. *(since 1.5.0)*
- `let p: [Int]` — Row permutation applied during pivoting. `p[i]` is the original index of the row now occupying position `i`, so `(P · b)[i] == b[p[i]]`. *(since 1.5.0)*
- `let permutationSign: Double` — Sign contributed by the row swaps: `+1` for an even number of swaps, `-1` for an odd number. Used to recover the determinant. *(since 1.5.0)*
- `var determinant: Double { get }` — The determinant of the original matrix, recovered as the permutation sign times the product of the diagonal of `U`. *(since 1.5.0)*
- `func solve(_ b: [Double]) -> [Double]` — Solves `A · x = b` using the stored factorization. Returns: The solution vector `x`. *(since 1.5.0)*

## LogDeterminant

`struct LogDeterminant` — Represents the sign and natural logarithm of a matrix determinant.

- `let sign: Double` — The sign of the determinant: -1, 0, or 1
- `let logAbsValue: Double` — The natural logarithm of the absolute determinant value
- `var value: Double { get }` — Reconstructs the determinant value (sign times exp of log absolute value)

## EigenDecomposition

`struct EigenDecomposition` — The result of a symmetric eigendecomposition. *(since 1.6.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `let eigenvalues: [Double]` — Eigenvalues sorted in descending order. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let eigenvectors: [[Double]]` — Orthonormal eigenvectors, one per row. Row `k` pairs with `eigenvalues[k]`. Each eigenvector is sign-fixed so its largest-magnitude element is positive. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let sweepsUsed: Int` — The number of full Jacobi sweeps the solver performed. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let converged: Bool` — Whether the off-diagonal norm reached the convergence tolerance within the sweep limit. An unconverged result is still a valid decomposition — the iterates remain exactly orthogonal-similar to the input — but its off-diagonal residual is larger than the tolerance guarantees. *(since 1.6.0)*

## MatrixError

`enum MatrixError` — Errors thrown by matrix operations that can fail at runtime.

Conforms to: Equatable, Error, Hashable.

- `case notSquare` — The operation requires a square matrix but received a non-square one.
- `case singular` — The matrix is singular (determinant = 0) and cannot be inverted.
- `case notSymmetric` — The operation requires a symmetric matrix but received an asymmetric one. *(since 1.6.0)*

## Array extensions where Element == [Fraction]

- `func asExpression() -> String` — Returns the matrix of fractions as a string, with each cell rendered by `asExpression()` and each column right-aligned to its widest entry. Returns: The matrix of fractions as a Unicode-formatted string. *(since 1.3.0)*

## Array extensions where Element == Double

- `func asExpression(form: VectorForm = .column) -> String` — Returns the vector as a string, with each entry formatted by the shared `UnicodeMath.formatCell` rules (NaN, ±∞, small magnitudes, integers all render predictably). Returns: The vector as a Unicode-formatted string. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `func asFractions(maxDenominator: Int = 1000) -> [Fraction]` — Converts each element to its simplest fractional representation. Returns: An array of `Fraction` values

## Array extensions where Element == Fraction

- `func asExpression(form: VectorForm = .column) -> String` — Returns the vector of fractions as a string, with each entry rendered by `asExpression()` and right-aligned so numerators and denominators line up vertically. Returns: The vector of fractions as a Unicode-formatted string. *(since 1.3.0)*

## VectorForm

`enum VectorForm` — The visual form a vector takes when rendered via `asExpression()`. *(since 1.3.0)*

Conforms to: Equatable, Hashable.

- `case column` — Column form with stacked Unicode brackets — the textbook default. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `case inline` — Inline angle-bracket form, `⟨a, b, c⟩` — the prose-friendly variant. *(since 1.3.0)*

## Fraction

`struct Fraction` — A rational number representation for educational display of numeric results.

Conforms to: Equatable.

- `let numerator: Int` — The numerator of the fraction
- `let denominator: Int` — The denominator of the fraction (always positive)
- `var value: Double { get }` — The floating-point value of this fraction
- `func asExpression() -> String` — Returns the fraction as a string in `a/b` form, or as a bare integer when the denominator is `1`. Returns: The fraction as a string. *(since 1.3.0)*
- `init(numerator: Int, denominator: Int)` — Creates a fraction from an explicit numerator and denominator
- `init(_ value: Double, maxDenominator: Int = 1000, tolerance: Double = 1e-9)` — Converts a Double to its simplest fractional representation using continued fraction expansion.

## Double extensions

- `func asFraction(maxDenominator: Int = 1000) -> Fraction` — Converts this value to its simplest fractional representation. Returns: A `Fraction` representing this value
